svg.title: Energy overview
svg.desc: Stores → transfers: Energy is conserved. Stores include kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, chemical and nuclear. Transfers: mechanically, electrically, by heating or radiation. Light and sound are not stores. Calculate store changes: Eₖ = ½mv²; Eₚ = mgΔh; Eₑ = ½ke². Use kg, m, m/s and N/m. Spring: extension, not total length; stay within proportional limit. Doubling v or e quadruples energy. Power & efficiency: P = E/t = W/t. Watts = joules per second. Same work in less time → greater power. Efficiency = useful output / total input; ×100 for %. Dissipated energy is less useful, not destroyed. Heating & insulation: ΔE = mcΔθ. Temperature change, not final temperature. Measure mass, energy and temperature rise. Insulation: low conductivity and greater thickness reduce transfer. Compare cooling with controls. Resources & reliability: Non-renewable: coal, oil, gas, nuclear. Renewable: biofuel, wind, Sun, tides, waves, hydro, geothermal. Uses: heating, transport, electricity. Wind/Sun vary; tides are predictable but not continuous. Evaluate a choice: Compare emissions, waste, habitat effects, cost, reliability and suitable sites. A resource mix helps match demand. Science informs decisions; economic and social choices matter.
